# credentials

engine credentials: subscriptions and API keys

Manage subscriptions and API keys, one per variable in each scope. Your personal ones are yours alone; workspace ones serve every member, and only owners and admins change them. A task runs on its requester's own, else the workspace's.

## `credentials list [--server <server>] [--yes] [--json]`

list your keys and the workspace keys, by variable

- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server, in the saved workspace
- `--yes` connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output

## `credentials add [--env <env>] [--value <value>] [--workspace] [--no-check] [--server <server>] [--yes] [--json]`

store an API key or subscription for one variable

Store the key of one environment variable, encrypted on the server, as your own or with --workspace for every member. A key saved for that variable in the same scope is replaced. Where the server has subscription sign-in on, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN takes your own claude setup-token output.

- `--env <env>` the variable tasks read the key as (reads that variable by default)
- `--value <value>` literal values land in shell history and are visible to other processes; use - for stdin or prefer environment variables
- `--workspace` a workspace key; owners and admins only
- `--no-check` skip the provider key check
- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server, in the saved workspace
- `--yes` connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output

```sh
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... coder credentials add --env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY  # your own Claude key, read from the environment
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... coder credentials add --env OPENAI_API_KEY --workspace  # a workspace key every member's tasks can use
pbpaste | coder credentials add --env OPENROUTER_API_KEY --value -  # a key for custom models, value from stdin
```

## `credentials login [engine] [--server <server>] [--yes] [--json]`

sign in to a claude or codex subscription on the server

Runs the official claude or codex sign-in on the server's runner, prints the sign-in link or device code, and waits. Claude asks you to paste the code the sign-in page shows. The result replaces your subscription for that engine. Needs CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTIONS=1 or CODEX_SUBSCRIPTIONS=1 on the server.

- `<engine>` claude or codex
- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server, in the saved workspace
- `--yes` connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output

## `credentials remove <NAME> [--workspace] [--server <server>] [--yes] [--json]`

remove the key of one variable

Remove the key of one environment variable.

- `<NAME>` the variable
- `--workspace` the workspace key of that variable
- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server, in the saved workspace
- `--yes` connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output
